newsitem.title: USA: BAB Holdings to buy Chesapeake Bagel.
newsitem.headline: BAB Holdings to buy Chesapeake Bagel.

text.p: BAB Holdings Inc, the operator of Big Apple Bagels, said Thursday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire the companies that own and operate the Chesapeake Bagel Bakery chain.

BAB said it expects to purchase the chain for about $29 million, including $22 million in cash, 900,000 shares of newly issued BAB common stock, and additional consideration based on future openings of new Chesapeake units already in development.
The transaction would be financed with a combination of debt and private equity, BAB said.
In June, BAB said it signed a letter of intent with Chesapeake but did not disclose terms.
BAB said it expects BAB's fiscal 1996 revenues, excluding the Chesapeake acquisition, to more than triple its fiscal 1995 revenues.

Chesapeake is expected to make a substantial contribution to BAB's revenues beginning in fiscal 1997, the company said, but the acquisition, depending on its closing date, is not likely to add significantly to revenues for the fiscal year ended November 30, 1996.
BAB said it expects to complete the transaction by calendar year-end or sooner, and believes that, on a fully diluted basis, the transaction will be anti-dilutive to earnings.

The two companies combined would give BAB Holdings a total of 285 units in 32 states, the District of Columbia and Canada, including 19 company-owned stores. For the two companies combined, BAB expects systemwide revenues of more than $100 million by its November fiscal year-end.
BAB said it plans to expand both Big Apple Bagels and Chesapeake Bagel Bakery and expects other smaller-sized acquisitions.
